title: delhi to lucknow bus diwali chhath
summary: Timings, fares, boarding points and drop locations for the Delhi to Lucknow bus during the Diwali and Chhath travel weeks of November 2026.
body_markdown:
This corridor behaves differently in the first half of November than it does for the rest of the year. Departures on the Delhi to Lucknow route run almost entirely in the evening, which means the festive squeeze lands on a narrow band of roughly seven hours of departure slots, twice in the same fortnight. Knowing which nights those are is most of the planning.


# The Corridor Through a Festive November


Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026, and the Chhath arghya on Sunday, 15 November, so the route carries two outbound waves and two return waves inside a single month rather than one continuous rush.


What follows covers the practical shape of the journey: distance and duration, the departure window, fare behaviour, boarding choices in the capital and drop points across[Lucknow and its wider route network](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/lucknow-bus-booking-online) , along with onward travel for anyone continuing east.


### Travelling the Delhi to Lucknow Bus Diwali Chhath Season


Anyone booking the Delhi to Lucknow bus Diwali Chhath season is competing for the same evening departures as families heading home for both festivals, and often for onward connections to Gorakhpur, Ayodhya, Varanasi and Bihar beyond Lucknow itself.


## Which Nights Fill First on This Route


Outbound pressure does not sit on the festival days. It sits on the two or three evenings before each of them, when working travellers leave after their last day at office.


- Diwali outbound: the evenings of 5, 6 and 7 November, with 7 November the tightest departure of the month.
- Diwali return: 10 and 11 November, once Bhai Dooj is over.
- Chhath outbound: 12 and 13 November, as Nahay Khay begins on 13 November.
- Chhath return: the evening of 16 November and all of 17 November, immediately after the Usha Arghya.


Between 8 and 11 November the corridor is comparatively easy, which is useful if your leave is flexible. Travelling out on the Sunday evening of Diwali itself is the least contested option in the whole window, though it does mean spending the festival on the road.


### Distance, Duration and What the Corridor Passes Through


The journey is long enough to need an overnight service and short enough to finish before the working day starts at the other end.


**Detail** **Current listing**


Distance Approximately 535 km


Journey time About 8 hours on the quicker services, with an average closer to 9 hours listed across the route


Daily departures 12 direct buses


Departure window 4:40 PM to 11:55 PM


Coach types Bharat Benz AC seater and sleeper, Ashok Leyland AC sleeper and seater, Volvo 9600 SLX multi axle AC sleeper


The corridor runs out of Delhi through Noida and Jewar, past Agra, and then east through Kannauj and Kanpur before the final stretch into Lucknow. That eastern section matters in festive weeks because Kanpur adds its own traffic to the same highway, and delays picked up there carry straight into your arrival time.


Because journey time figures differ slightly between the summary panel and the route description, treat both as indicative and check the duration shown against the specific departure you select on the[Delhi to Lucknow route page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-lucknow-bus-route) for your date.


### What Fares Look Like on This Corridor


Listed fares on the route currently run from about Rs 367 at the lower end up to around Rs 1,221, with the spread reflecting coach type, seat position and how much of the bus has already sold.


In the Diwali and Chhath weeks the lower end of that range disappears first. It is not a separate festive tariff so much as the cheaper coaches and the less popular seats selling out early, leaving the premium sleeper inventory. Booking through the second half of October keeps the whole range available to you rather than the top of it.


**Note:** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## Choosing a Boarding Point in Delhi NCR


This route offers a wide spread of pickups, and the right one depends less on distance than on how reliably you can reach it on a festival evening.


- Kashmere Gate ISBT: the counter sits inside the terminal near the metro exit, which makes it the most weather proof and crowd proof option for anyone arriving by metro.
- Anand Vihar ISBT: convenient from east Delhi and Ghaziabad, with a counter inside the terminal building.
- Akshardham: a roadside boarding point near the DTC stand, useful from south and central Delhi but exposed to evening traffic on the flyover approach.
- Dhaula Kuan and Jhandewalan: practical for west and central Delhi travellers who want to avoid crossing the city to reach a terminal.
- Noida International Airport at Jewar: worth considering if you are already on that side, since the bus passes it early in the run.


Several other pickups across Rohini, Pitampura, Faridabad and the Dwarka side operate as cab transfers to the main coach. Those are convenient in normal weeks. On a festival evening, when the connecting cab is moving through the same congestion as everyone else, a terminal boarding point is the steadier choice.


## Where the Bus Actually Sets You Down in Lucknow


Drop points on this corridor are spread along the approach to the city rather than concentrated in the centre, and that catches people who assume they will be left near Hazratganj.


Common drops include Kamta Bypass on Shaheed Path, Transport Nagar, Nahariya Chauraha, Mohan Zero Point and the stop near GITM, along with Lucknow Medical College towards Barabanki. Each of these needs an auto or taxi for the last leg, so check which one is closest to your final address before you select it during booking, and keep a local number handy for a 6 AM arrival.


For travellers continuing to a smaller town in eastern Uttar Pradesh or Bihar, this is the decision that saves the most time. A drop on the correct side of the city can remove an hour of cross town travel before your onward journey even begins.


## Meals and Onboard Conditions on an Overnight Run


Delhi to Lucknow is one of the three corridors, along with Delhi to Gorakhpur and Chennai to Coimbatore, where the Freemeal offer applies on Plus buses through the relevant coupon code at checkout. This is a route specific offer and is not available network wide.


Separately, Food on Bus lets you pre-book a vegetarian meal during checkout or later from the My Trip section of the app, with items priced from about Rs 99. A marshal serves it at your seat. The two are different things: one is an offer attached to specific routes, the other is a paid onboard meal service you order in advance.


Coaches on the route list charging points, blankets, water bottles, live tracking and an onboard washroom, with bio toilets on several services. Baggage is capped at 15 kg per passenger, which is easy to exceed when you are carrying sweets and gifts for a family visit.


## Continuing East From Lucknow


Lucknow works well as a staging point rather than a final stop during these weeks. For travellers heading to the ghats for Chhath or to Kashi for Dev Deepawali on 24 November, the Lucknow to Varanasi bus route covers the next leg in around five hours with several departures through the day.


Plan this connection with a gap rather than a tight transfer. An overnight bus that loses 90 minutes to festive highway traffic will not make a morning onward departure, and the second leg in a peak week is exactly the seat you cannot rebook on the spot.


## The Return Leg Deserves Equal Attention


Return travel from Lucknow is the harder booking of the two. Departures on the[Lucknow to Delhi bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/lucknow-to-delhi-bus-route) run across a wider spread of the day than the outbound leg, but demand on 10, 11, 16 and 17 November compresses into the same evening slots.


If your return date is uncertain, check the cancellation terms attached to your fare before booking rather than after. Holding a seat you might change costs less than finding one on the busiest return night of the month.


## Settling the Festive Delhi to Lucknow Plan


The corridor itself is straightforward: an evening departure, a highway run through Agra and Kanpur, and an early morning arrival on the outskirts of Lucknow. What changes in November is the margin for error, because there are only twelve departures a day and four nights on which most people want them.


Pick the boarding point you can reach without depending on traffic, pick the drop point closest to where you are actually going, and book the return in the same session. Do those three things by the end of October and the Delhi to Lucknow bus Diwali Chhath trip becomes ordinary travel rather than a scramble.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How long does the Delhi to Lucknow bus journey take?


The Delhi to Lucknow bus journey takes about 8 to 9 hours across roughly 535 km, depending on the departure selected and highway traffic.


### What time do Delhi to Lucknow buses depart?


Delhi to Lucknow buses depart between 4:40 PM and 11:55 PM, which makes this an overnight corridor with early morning arrivals into the city.


### What is the fare on the Delhi to Lucknow bus?


Fares on the Delhi to Lucknow bus currently run from about Rs 367 up to around Rs 1,221, depending on coach type, seat and date.


### When should I book the Delhi to Lucknow bus Diwali Chhath travel?


Book the Delhi to Lucknow bus Diwali Chhath travel through the second half of October, since the cheaper inventory on peak evenings sells out first.


### Which are the busiest travel dates on this route in November 2026?


The busiest dates are 6 and 7 November before Diwali, 12 and 13 November before Chhath, and 16 and 17 November for returns.


### How many buses run daily between Delhi and Lucknow?


Twelve direct buses currently run daily between Delhi and Lucknow, all departing within the evening window rather than across the full day.


### Which boarding point in Delhi is most convenient?


Kashmere Gate ISBT is usually the most convenient boarding point because the counter sits inside the terminal close to the metro exit.


### Where do buses drop passengers in Lucknow?


Buses drop passengers at points including Kamta Bypass, Transport Nagar, Nahariya Chauraha and Mohan Zero Point, each needing a short onward transfer.


### Is a meal included on the Delhi to Lucknow route?


Delhi to Lucknow is one of three routes where the Freemeal offer applies on Plus buses, and paid Food on Bus meals can be pre booked separately.


### Is a washroom available on this route?


A washroom is available on this route, with bio toilets fitted on several of the coaches operating between Delhi and Lucknow.


### How much luggage is allowed?


Luggage is capped at 15 kg per passenger, which is worth checking when you are carrying festival sweets, gifts and extra clothing.


### Can I continue from Lucknow to Varanasi by bus?


You can continue from Lucknow to Varanasi by bus in around five hours, though a comfortable gap between the two legs is advisable.


### Are women only seats available on this corridor?


Women only seating can be selected at checkout on this corridor, and live tracking is available through the app for the full journey.
